PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral Blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Tay-Sachs disease

TEST PERFORMED
HEXA Gene Sequencing

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. Targeted sequencing of the HEXA gene was performed covering the entire coding region and splice sites. All 14 exons and flanking intronic sequences were amplified by PCR and sequenced bidirectionally using Sanger sequencing methodology. Sequence data was analyzed and compared to the reference sequence HEXA NM_000520.4 (NCBI RefSeq).

Technical Note: This analysis detects point mutations and small insertions/deletions within the coding regions and splice sites of the HEXA gene. Large deletions, duplications, or rearrangements would not be detected by this methodology. Deletion/duplication analysis was not performed as part of this test.

RESULTS
Gene: HEXA (NM_000520.4)
Result: No pathogenic variants detected

No mutations were identified in the HEXA gene by DNA sequencing. All coding exons and splice sites showed normal sequence.

INTERPRETATION
No HEXA mutations were identified by sequencing analysis. This result significantly reduces but does not eliminate the possibility of Tay-Sachs disease in this patient. Approximately 95% of pathogenic variants in the HEXA gene are detectable by sequencing; however, deep intronic variants, large deletions/duplications, or complex rearrangements would not be detected by this method.

LIMITATIONS
- This test does not detect large deletions or duplications of the HEXA gene
- Deep intronic variants outside the regions analyzed are not detected
- Variants in regulatory regions are not assessed
- No additional mutation analysis is currently available through our laboratory

RECOMMENDATIONS
If clinical suspicion for Tay-Sachs disease remains high, consider:
- Hexosaminidase A enzyme activity testing
- Deletion/duplication analysis of the HEXA gene if available through specialized laboratories
- Clinical correlation with patient presentation

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted name] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
